overview: These settings shape how effects and some shikigami attacks launch, steer, fall, slide along the ground, and leave a second effect behind.
description: Effect/shikigami movement profiles used by AGameEffect::Initialize and fetched directly by CN_* action controllers: launch aiming, speed easing, homing, optional tilt, ground following and an optional child ground effect.

ID.simple: The name the game uses to connect an effect or shikigami attack to this movement setup.
ID.technical: FName row key (export column 'ID', native UPROPERTY Id, import key Id; FName lookups are case-insensitive). AGameEffect::Initialize checks EffectRow.Id_EffectMove, resolves it against manager slot +0x690 with an inlined first-match UDataTable::FindRow (bWarnIfMissing=false; retail Initialize 0x131f290) and passes the result to UGameEffectMovementController::Start (retail 0x135cba0). None or a name with no row leaves movement unstarted. One exported shard with 147 distinct rows. 149 Effect rows name an EffectMove row (114 distinct IDs) and all resolve; other rows are fetched by name from CN_* controllers (28 have a literal C++ call site in the current reconstruction; five have no identified C++ use).

EffectMoveType.simple: Chooses whether the effect starts ahead of itself, toward the target, or toward a chosen spot.
EffectMoveType.technical: EGameEffectMoveType : uint8 (0 None, 1 Straight, 2 Target, 3 Location, 255 Invalid). Straight aims along the effect actor's own GetFacingForwardVector(); Target aims at Source->GetTargetLocation(Source->GetSecondaryTargetActor()), using a yaw/pitch basis from the source's auto-aim and root axes when either Limit_AngleXY or Limit_AngleZ is positive; Location uses Source->GetEffectMoveTargetLocation(). None/unhandled leaves the controller's current MoveDirection unchanged before the final normalization. Exports: 141 Straight, 6 Target, no None or Location rows.

MoveDirection.simple: Changes the travel direction compared with the chosen aim, including whether the effect rises or drops.
MoveDirection.technical: FVector (UE5 double components). AimAlong faces the effect with FRotationMatrix::MakeFromX(launch direction), then sets MoveDirection = that rotation rotated into the row vector (Rotation.RotateVector(Row->MoveDirection)); Start normalizes once after the type switch. Exports: 143 rows (1,0,0), two rows with Z=0.05/0.1, and two rows (0,0,-1). A zero row vector would leave movement at zero.

bHomingEnabled.simple: Turns on steering toward the target after launch, letting the effect follow the target as it moves.
bHomingEnabled.technical: bool. Start stores Source->GetSecondaryTargetActor() as HomingTarget. Each Update refreshes HomingTargetLocation from the source's GetTargetLocation(HomingTarget) only while not bHomingLocked (the lock is set when the target reports a status/action slot 66 within its range), then runs UpdateHomingXY/Z while Homing_Time permits. true selects the homing Update branch (tilt applies, Fall_AngularVelocityZ and along-ground sliding do not); the child ground effect check is outside both branches. Exports: 112 true, 35 false.

Speed_Start.simple: The speed the effect or shikigami attack starts with. A bigger number makes the opening movement faster.
Speed_Start.technical: float, UE units/s. StartValue of FGameFloatEaseInterpolator::Start(From, To, Duration, EaseType, Exponent, InSteps=2): FloatInterp38.Start(Speed_Start, Speed_End, Speed_InterpolateTime, ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc(Speed_EasingType), Speed_Blend_Exp, 2). Direct shikigami action consumers copy the same five row values into their own ease (CN_050, CN_180, CN_220, CN_231, CN_270, CN_280). Export sample: 6000.0.

Speed_End.simple: The speed the effect or shikigami attack reaches as the move continues. Bigger numbers make the later movement faster.
Speed_End.technical: float, UE units/s. TargetValue of the same interpolator; direct shikigami action consumers read it with the other Speed_* fields. Export sample: 4500.0.

Speed_InterpolateTime.simple: How long the move takes to change from its starting speed to its ending speed. Longer times make the change more gradual.
Speed_InterpolateTime.technical: float seconds, the interpolator Duration. Update clamps Elapsed at Duration, so once elapsed the current speed remains Speed_End; two exported rows use 0.0 and are immediately at the target. Export sample: 0.5.

Speed_EasingType.simple: Shapes how the speed changes over time, whether it eases in or out. Even the plain setting eases out.
Speed_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType : uint8 (0 None, 1 EaseIn, 2 EaseOut, 3 EaseInOut, 255 Invalid). ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc (retail 0x1412fa480) maps EaseIn/EaseOut/EaseInOut directly and maps None and all other values to EEasingFunc::EaseOut, not Linear. Exports: 114 None (therefore EaseOut at runtime), 32 EaseOut, 1 EaseIn, no EaseInOut.

Speed_Blend_Exp.simple: Changes how strongly the speed curve bends. Bigger values make the speed change feel more pronounced.
Speed_Blend_Exp.technical: float passed as the interpolator's InExponent, used by the EaseIn/EaseOut/EaseInOut branches (including the EaseOut produced from None). The final literal 2 is InSteps and is only used by EEasingFunc::Step. Export values are 1.0, 2.0 and 4.0.

Delay_Time.simple: How long the effect waits before it starts moving. Longer waits hold it in place for more time.
Delay_Time.technical: float seconds. Start stores UE_KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER when Delay_Time<=0, otherwise the row value; Update decrements DelayTime and returns while it is >0, so non-positive values consume only one negligible delay step. Exports: 141 rows 0.0, five 0.05, one 0.07.

Fall_AngularVelocityZ.simple: Sets how fast the path bends downward during a falling phase in one shikigami's attacks. Bigger values make the arc turn faster.
Fall_AngularVelocityZ.technical: float degrees/second. In UGameEffectMovementController it is read only in the non-homing branch: when >0 MoveDirection is rotated about the effect's current local-right axis by DeltaSeconds * value and the actor quaternion is rebuilt via MakeFromXY. All 10 exported rows with 60.0 also have bHomingEnabled=true, so the effect controller never applies the field to those shipped rows; CN_231_ActionController independently applies the same rotation during its attack phase using this row. The other 137 rows are 0.0.

Limit_AngleXY.simple: Limits how far the move can aim or steer sideways from its intended direction. Bigger numbers allow wider side angles.
Limit_AngleXY.technical: float degrees. For EffectMoveType::Target with either limit positive, the initial direction is clamped around the source's auto-aim yaw by this angle. During homing, UpdateHomingXY returns when the XY angle to the target is >= Limit_AngleXY (when >0). Values <=0 disable that clamp; exports include 13 zeros and six -1 sentinels. Export sample: 40.0.

Limit_AngleZ.simple: Limits how far the move can aim or steer above or below its intended direction. Bigger numbers allow wider up-and-down angles.
Limit_AngleZ.technical: float degrees. With either initial limit positive, Start caps the computed vertical misalignment from the source's auto-aim at this value when Limit_AngleZ>0; UpdateHomingZ likewise returns when the elevation angle is >= Limit_AngleZ. <=0 disables the vertical cap; exports include eight zeros and six -1 sentinels. Export sample: 40.0.

Homing_AngularVelocityXY.simple: How fast the effect or shikigami attack turns left or right to follow the target. Bigger values turn more quickly.
Homing_AngularVelocityXY.technical: float degrees/second. UpdateHomingXY returns when <=0; otherwise it steps MoveDirection by DeltaSeconds * rate toward the target's XY bearing (sign from the 2D cross product), clamped to the remaining angle and suppressed past Limit_AngleXY. Export sample: 1.0; 13 rows use 0.0 to disable XY steering.

Homing_AngularVelocityZ.simple: How fast the effect or shikigami attack turns up or down to follow the target. Bigger values turn more quickly.
Homing_AngularVelocityZ.technical: float degrees/second. UpdateHomingZ transforms the target into effect-local space, measures elevation and rotates MoveDirection about the horizontal axis 90 degrees from it (the effect-local right in the XY plane) by DeltaSeconds * rate toward the target, clamped to the angle and Limit_AngleZ. Export sample: 1.0; nine rows use 0.0 to disable Z steering.

Homing_Time.simple: How long the move keeps steering toward the target. Longer times keep the chase going, and zero means no limit.
Homing_Time.technical: float seconds. HomingElapsed starts at 0 and increments while !(HomingElapsed > Homing_Time && Homing_Time > 0); once that fails, XY/Z steering stops but movement continues. 62 exported rows use 0.0 (unlimited homing); the maximum is 3.0.

bTilt.simple: Turns on the lean into turns while an effect follows its target. This setting is off in every listed move.
bTilt.technical: bool; only consumed in the homing Update branch. The 2D angle between previous and new direction *10 (capped at 30 degrees, signed by the cross product) becomes a roll offset that approaches/leaves at 60 degrees per second (TiltRoll). All 147 exported rows are false.

bAlongGroundEnabled.simple: Turns on ground sliding for effects that are not steering toward a target.
bAlongGroundEnabled.technical: bool; only used in the non-homing Update branch. Six exported rows enable it (CP_050_ATTACKH_01_01, four CP_260_ATTACKC/D_02_01_* rows and CN_250_ATTACKG_01_01). MoveAlongGround performs up to 10 capsule sweeps of radius AlongGroundHeight*mean actor scale, projects direction along hit normals (slopes above 65 degrees are ignored), then line-probes downward. Rotation alignment is additionally gated by the controller's non-row bGroundAlignedRotation flag, which CP_260 sets on the spawned effects that use four of these rows.

bAlongGroundDownEnabled.simple: Makes ground-following effects check farther down and accept any ground surface they find.
bAlongGroundDownEnabled.technical: bool used only by MoveAlongGround: doubles the downward probe depth when bOnGround is set, and determines the ground-acceptance test (true accepts any filtered ground hit; false requires Dot(ImpactNormal, MoveDirection) < -0.0). Five exported rows enable it.

bIsStoppedOnAir.simple: Ends a ground-following effect when it cannot find ground beneath it. This only matters when ground sliding is on.
bIsStoppedOnAir.technical: bool; at the end of MoveAlongGround, when the filtered downward probe reports no ground hits the effect actor is finished. Only reachable with bAlongGroundEnabled=true; four exported rows enable it.

AlongGroundHeight.simple: Sets how far around the effect the game checks for ground while it slides. Bigger values let it follow ground from farther away.
AlongGroundHeight.technical: float multiplied by the mean of the effect actor's XYZ scale ((X+Y+Z)/3) to form both the capsule sweep radius and the downward probe depth (doubled when bAlongGroundDownEnabled && bOnGround). 141 exported rows are 0.0; CP_050_ATTACKH_01_01 uses 25.0, the four CP_260 ground rows use 100.0 and CN_250_ATTACKG_01_01 uses 150.0.

Id_Effect_AlongGround.simple: Names the extra effect that appears on the ground beneath a moving effect. Only one listed move uses it.
Id_Effect_AlongGround.technical: FName; skipped when None. Only CP_050_ATTACKH_01_01 sets it, to FX_CP_050_09116 (present in EffectDataTable with PoolCount=0). UpdateAlongGroundEffect is called after either movement branch, independently of bAlongGroundEnabled/bHomingEnabled: it line-traces downward by AlongGroundEffect_Height * mean actor scale; on a hit it resolves this ID to an Effect row, spawns/initializes its FileName_BP (pooled only when that row's PoolCount>0), places it at ImpactPoint and orients it to the hit normal plus travel direction. On a miss an existing child is finished and cleared.

AlongGroundEffect_Height.simple: Sets how far below the moving effect the game looks for ground before placing the extra effect. Bigger values search farther down.
AlongGroundEffect_Height.technical: float multiplied by the effect's mean actor scale to determine the End point of the line trace in UpdateAlongGroundEffect. Only read when Id_Effect_AlongGround is not None: 50.0 on CP_050_ATTACKH_01_01, 0.0 on the other 146 rows.

notes: EffectMoveDataTables is manager slot +0x690 (FGameDataTableArray); the single table is registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:407 and loaded into that slot at line 235.

In UGameEffectMovementController the row has two largely exclusive branches: homing (bHomingEnabled with bTilt and Homing_* steering) and non-homing (Fall_AngularVelocityZ plus optional along-ground sliding). Speed/delay, launch aiming and the optional child ground effect are common to both.

The same row struct is cached as MoveRow (+0x190) by shikigami action controllers CN_050, CN_180, CN_220, CN_231, CN_270 and CN_280 via CN_280_FindEffectMoveRow. They use Speed_* for their own ease and Homing_* (and, in CN_231, Fall_AngularVelocityZ) for character motion; they do not start UGameEffectMovementController. GameCharacterMovementController and GameShikigamiMovementController use similarly named fields from different row structs (ActionHoming/ActionMove/ActionDash), not this table.

Missing or None IDs behave differently by caller: the effect path passes nullptr to Start, which safely returns, while direct shikigami callers usually dereference the finder result immediately without a null check.

CP_260 sets controller bGroundAlignedRotation=1 on the effect actors spawned with four ground-following rows, enabling the rotation alignment inside MoveAlongGround; that flag is not a row field and Start otherwise clears it.

No localization variants or numbered shards exist in the export; the 147 rows are distinct named movement profiles. No Blueprint or retail runtime observations were available: behavioral statements come from the current C++ reconstruction (whose comments carry static retail RVA annotations) and from the exported values.
The speed interpolator treats EGameEasingType::None as EEasingFunc::EaseOut, so the EaseOut sample and the 114 None rows both use Speed_Blend_Exp as an easing exponent.

usages.detail: Effect initialization resolves Id_EffectMove through the manager's EffectMoveDataTables and starts UGameEffectMovementController with the row (Start at retail 0x135cba0); None or a missed lookup leaves movement unstarted (retail Initialize 0x131f290).
Start chooses the launch direction from EffectMoveType, source/target/location and limit angles, then arms homing, speed and delay.
Update applies homing/tilt or fall/ground movement, advances the speed ease, moves the actor and updates the ground child effect.
MoveAlongGround implements the bAlongGroundEnabled/DownEnabled/StopOnAir and AlongGroundHeight behavior (retail 0x14133A590).
A non-effect consumer fetches an EffectMove row by name and uses its speed curve for shikigami character actions (retail 0x141463CE0).
CN_231 applies Fall_AngularVelocityZ from its cached EffectMove row during an attack phase, independently of the effect controller's homing branch.
Indirect use: CP_260 enables ground-aligned rotation on spawned effects whose Effect rows point at the ground-following EffectMove rows.
